profile.research_note:
Operator attribution to Visa is doubtful: Visa own documented architecture centers on Denver and Ashburn, not Vernon Hills IL; a lead-level source associates this address with AT&T instead. Flagged for a facility-level operator verification pass rather than reassigned now.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is located in Vernon Hills, Illinois, a Chicago suburb, and is attributed to Visa Inc., the global payments technology company headquartered in San Francisco, California. Visa own published materials describe a dual data center architecture for its core VisaNet payment processing network, with primary facilities in the Denver, Colorado area and the Ashburn, Virginia area, providing geographic redundancy for global transaction processing; this Vernon Hills location was not corroborated by Visa own site or by Wikipedia. The only references found for a Vernon Hills data center address were an Illinois State Fire Marshal underground storage tank registry entry and a business directory listing showing the address associated with AT&T rather than Visa specifically, both lower tier lead level sources. Because Visa documented architecture centers on the Denver and Ashburn facilities, this Vernon Hills attribution should be treated with caution as possibly a misattributed AT&T or other carrier facility, or a smaller regional office, rather than confirmed Visa production data center. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
No published power or capacity specifications exist for this facility. The address is verified to a real location in Vernon Hills, Illinois, but operator attribution to Visa is uncertain; research notes flag the site as possibly an AT&T facility or smaller regional office rather than a Visa production data center, and Visa's documented architecture centers instead on Denver and Ashburn facilities.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, of which only six publish power specifications totaling 236 MW. This facility would rank seventh by published capacity in the state if its specifications were public, but they are not disclosed.

Without published power or technical specifications, this campus cannot be evaluated for significance to AI infrastructure scaling. The operator attribution itself requires facility-level verification before any reading of capacity or capability is possible.
